children.name: PRD Title
children.characters: NEXT.JS MOBILE PRODUCT — PRODUCT REQUIREMENTS DOCUMENT

children.name: Subtitle
children.characters: iPhone-first / Instagram-inspired interaction model / premium editorial visual language

children.name: 01 — PRODUCT INTENT Body
children.characters: Build a premium mobile web experience in Next.js that feels native on iPhone: edge-to-edge content, thumb-reachable controls, fast transitions, minimal chrome, strong visual hierarchy, and a polished content-first feed.

children.name: 02 — TARGET PLATFORM Body
children.characters: Primary viewport: 390×844 CSS px (iPhone 14/15 class). Support 375–430 px widths. Desktop is secondary and should widen into a centered app shell without changing core interactions.

children.name: 03 — INFORMATION ARCHITECTURE Body
children.characters: Bottom navigation: Home / Discover / Create / Activity / Profile. Primary feed is vertically scrollable. Detail views preserve back navigation. Create opens a focused composer. Profile uses a tabbed gallery/list pattern.

children.name: 04 — CORE UX FLOWS Body
children.characters: Launch → Home feed → open content → detail → like/save/share/comment → return to feed. Search → result list → profile/content. Create → media selection → edit metadata → publish → success state. Profile → content grid → detail.

children.name: 05 — VISUAL SYSTEM Body
children.characters: Palette: warm off-white background, near-black typography, restrained gray surfaces, one signature accent used sparingly for active states. Use generous whitespace and subtle 1 px dividers instead of heavy cards.

children.name: 06 — TYPOGRAPHY Body
children.characters: Primary UI: Inter. Display/editorial: a refined serif such as Instrument Serif or Cormorant Garamond where available. Avoid more than two font families. H1 32/38, section title 22/28, body 15/22, meta 12/16, buttons 14/18 semibold.

children.name: 07 — COMPONENTS Body
children.characters: AppShell, TopBar, BottomNav, StoryRail, FeedCard, MediaViewer, Avatar, IconButton, LikeButton, SaveButton, CommentSheet, ShareSheet, SearchBar, FilterPills, ProfileHeader, GalleryGrid, Composer, Toast, SkeletonLoader, EmptyState, ErrorState.

children.name: 08 — INTERACTION Body
children.characters: Tap targets ≥44 px. Bottom nav remains fixed. Sheets use spring-like 220–320 ms transitions. Content opens with shared-element style continuity where practical. Buttons have press scale ~0.98. Respect prefers-reduced-motion.

children.name: 09 — NEXT.JS IMPLEMENTATION Body
children.characters: Use Next.js App Router + React Server Components by default. Client components only for interactive islands. Use route groups for app shell, dynamic routes for content/profile detail, loading.tsx for skeletons, error.tsx for recoverable failures, and next/image for optimized media.

children.name: 10 — DATA CONTRACTS Body
children.characters: Content: id, author, avatar, media, caption, createdAt, likes, comments, saved. User: id, handle, displayName, avatar, bio, followers, following. Actions are optimistic where safe, with rollback on error.

children.name: 11 — RESPONSIVE RULES Body
children.characters: At <768 px use bottom navigation and one-column media. At ≥768 px use a centered max-width shell with optional side navigation. Do not simply scale the mobile UI; preserve readable measure and comfortable hit areas.

children.name: 12 — ACCESSIBILITY Body
children.characters: Semantic buttons/links, visible focus styles, alt text for meaningful media, decorative media marked accordingly, reduced motion support, color contrast suitable for small text, form labels, keyboard access for all interactive controls.

children.name: 13 — PERFORMANCE Body
children.characters: Prioritize LCP media, use responsive image sizes, lazy-load below-the-fold content, avoid large client bundles, virtualize long feeds where justified, prefetch likely next routes, and keep transitions GPU-friendly.

children.name: 14 — ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA Body
children.characters: Feels native on iPhone Safari; no horizontal overflow; bottom nav never obscures content; all primary actions are reachable with one hand; loading and empty states are designed; typography remains legible at dynamic text sizes; animations do not block navigation.

children.name: 15 — DELIVERY PHASES Body
children.characters: Phase 1: shell + typography + feed. Phase 2: detail/profile/search. Phase 3: create/composer + sheets. Phase 4: performance/accessibility QA + analytics instrumentation. Phase 5: visual polish and device validation.

children.name: SCREEN SPEC — HOME FEED
children.characters: Header: logo/wordmark + activity action. Story rail below. Feed cards use edge-to-edge media, compact author row, action row, caption, and metadata. Keep visual density close to Instagram, but use a more editorial/premium tone through typography, spacing, and restrained surfaces.

children.name: SCREEN SPEC — DETAIL
children.characters: Full media viewer, persistent back action, author metadata, engagement actions, caption/comments preview, and a contextual next-content affordance. The detail screen should feel immersive, not like a modal.

children.name: SCREEN SPEC — PROFILE
children.characters: Profile header with avatar, display name, bio, stats, primary action, and segmented tabs. Default content view is a 3-column grid with 1 px gutters; selecting an item opens detail while preserving scroll position.

children.name: ENGINEERING NOTES
children.characters: Use CSS env(safe-area-inset-top/bottom). Keep bottom-nav padding above env(safe-area-inset-bottom). Avoid fixed heights for text-rich areas. Prefer CSS clamp for typography where helpful. Centralize tokens in globals.css and component-level CSS modules or an established styling system.

children.name: Subtitle
children.characters: Production roadmap — architecture → UI system → features → data → QA → launch

children.characters:
• Next.js App Router + TypeScript
• ESLint + Prettier + strict TS
• Environment variable strategy
• Git branching + PR conventions
• CI: typecheck, lint, build
• Error monitoring + analytics placeholders
• Deliverable: deployable shell with CI passing.

children.name: PHASE 1 — DESIGN SYSTEM + APP SHELL title
PHASE 1 — DESIGN SYSTEM + APP SHELL body
children.characters:
• Font loading and typography tokens
• Color, spacing, radius, shadow, motion tokens
• iPhone safe-area handling
• AppShell / TopBar / BottomNav
• IconButton, Avatar, Button, Divider
• Skeleton / Toast / Empty / Error primitives
• Validate 375 / 390 / 430 px
• Deliverable: reusable visual system and shell.

children.name: PHASE 2 — HOME FEED body
children.characters:
• Feed route + StoryRail + FeedCard
• Optimized responsive media
• Like / save / share interactions
• Optimistic UI
• Infinite or cursor pagination
• Loading, empty and error states
• Deliverable: complete iPhone feed.

children.name: PHASE 3 — CONTENT DETAIL body
children.characters:
• Dynamic content route
• Full media viewer
• Author metadata + engagement controls
• Caption/comments preview
• Share sheet
• Back navigation + scroll restoration
• Prefetch adjacent content
• Deliverable: seamless feed → detail → feed journey.

children.name: PHASE 4 — SEARCH + DISCOVERY body
children.characters:
• Debounced search
• Recent searches
• Filter chips
• Profile/content results
• URL-driven search state where practical
• Empty/error states
• Deliverable: fast discovery flow.

children.name: PHASE 5 — PROFILE body
children.characters:
• Profile header + stats
• Follow/unfollow
• Segmented tabs
• 3-column gallery
• Saved/private states where required
• Preserve gallery scroll position
• Deliverable: complete profile experience.

children.name: PHASE 6 — CREATE / PUBLISH body
children.characters:
• Media picker
• Preview/crop
• Caption + metadata
• Draft state
• Upload progress
• Publish API
• Success/failure recovery
• Deliverable: reliable publishing workflow.

children.name: PHASE 7 — DATA + BACKEND body
children.characters:
• Define API contracts / schemas
• Authentication/session
• User/content/comment models
• Cursor pagination
• Media storage
• Authorization + validation
• Rate limits
• Optimistic mutation rollback
• Deliverable: production data flow.

children.name: PHASE 8 — PERFORMANCE + ACCESSIBILITY body
children.characters:
• next/image priority and sizing
• Lazy loading below fold
• Reduce client component boundaries
• Bundle analysis
• Cache/prefetch strategy
• Keyboard + screen-reader QA
• Reduced motion
• Dynamic text-size validation
• Deliverable: performance/accessibility pass.

children.name: PHASE 9 — QA + DEVICE VALIDATION body
children.characters:
• iPhone Safari: 375 / 390 / 393 / 430 px
• iOS portrait + landscape where relevant
• Android Chrome baseline
• Desktop responsive shell
• Slow 4G / offline recovery
• Long captions/usernames
• Empty/error/loading states
• Rapid taps + repeated mutations
• Deep links + refresh
• Deliverable: release candidate with no P0/P1 defects.

children.name: PHASE 10 — LAUNCH + OBSERVABILITY body
children.characters:
• Production deployment
• Error tracking
• Analytics events
• Core Web Vitals
• Feature flags for risky features
• Post-deploy smoke tests
• Rollback procedure
• Post-launch triage
• Deliverable: monitored production release.

components/

children.name: ENGINEERING RULES
children.characters:
1. Server Components by default; Client Components only for state/browser APIs.
2. Keep domain logic out of presentational components.
3. Every mutation has loading + failure behavior.
4. Never depend on fixed viewport height for core content.
5. Use semantic HTML before ARIA.
6. Keep design tokens centralized.
7. Start with URL state + local React state; add a global store only when justified.
8. iPhone Safari is the primary acceptance environment.

children.name: DEFINITION OF DONE
children.characters: A feature is complete only when the approved Figma direction is implemented, responsive behavior is defined, loading/empty/error states exist, accessibility is covered, analytics are defined where needed, TypeScript/lint/build pass, mobile Safari is manually tested, and no P0/P1 issue remains.
